title: Collecting light in the shade: chloroplasts, grana, antenna

images.caption: Wood sorrel (Oxalis acetosella) carpeting the floor of a dark spruce forest, Estonia; horsetail in the sunfleck
images.credit: Maris Juuse 2012, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
images.note: Classic shade plant under a closed canopy; the dark trunks behind show how little light gets through.

images.caption: Dense old spruce stand, Sweden: bare lower branches, wood sorrel and ferns on the dim floor
images.note: The wide view: canopy shades the floor so strongly that the trees shed their own lower branches.

images.caption: Flowering wood sorrel covering a forest floor in spring, Münster, Germany
images.credit: Dietmar Rabich 2019, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
images.note: Close-up of the shade plant itself; works as the camera target of the zoom.

images.caption: Giant taro (Alocasia macrorrhizos) in dim subtropical rainforest understory, Lamington National Park, Australia
images.credit: John Robert McPherson 2013, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
images.note: Alocasia is the classic deep-shade plant of the grana literature (giant grana; Goodchild et al. 1972, Chow et al. 1988).

images.caption: Gustav Senn (1875–1945), Basel botanist who showed in 1908 how chloroplasts change shape and position with light
images.credit: Photopress AG, between 1915 and 1935; Universitätsbibliothek Basel, UBH Portr BS Senn G 1875, 2 (no licence stated in the record)
images.note: Closest and sharpest of four UB Basel portraits; scan colour chart cropped off. Best for a halftone avatar.

images.caption: Gustav Senn in 1933, signed portrait on its card mount
images.credit: Lafayette Ltd., 1933; Universitätsbibliothek Basel, UBH Portr BS Senn G 1875, 1b (no licence stated in the record)
images.note: Alternative: later, calmer portrait with his signature; scan colour chart cropped off.

images.caption: Senn's student drawing, 1895: chloroplasts moving in Vallisneria leaf cells, arrows show their paths
images.credit: G. Senn 1895, in Honegger 2022, Bauhinia 28:63, Abb. 3a (CC BY 4.0)

images.caption: A: chloroplast positions in dark, weak and strong light; B: matching Arabidopsis leaf sections; D: avoidance spelling 光 (light)
images.credit: Wada 2016, Proc Jpn Acad Ser B 92:387, Fig. 1 (CC BY)
images.note: The field’s own schematic of accumulation vs avoidance, next to real sections; only 758 px wide on PMC.

images.caption: Arabidopsis mesophyll after 1 h strong light, seen from above: wild type moves chloroplasts to side walls; phot2 mutant cannot
images.note: a: leaf transmittance rises with light as chloroplasts flee (WT, phot1) but not in phot2 or chup1; b at 500 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, scale 20 µm. Legend read on nature.com.

images.caption: Model organisms of chloroplast movement; B: Mougeotia ribbon chloroplast face-on (left) and edge-on (right), red chlorophyll fluorescence
images.credit: Wada 2016, Proc Jpn Acad Ser B 92:387, Fig. 2 (CC BY; panel B after the PNAS cover of 20 Sep 2005)
images.note: Only panel B (Mougeotia) is on topic, and it is small (figure 757 px wide); F is a TEM of chloroplasts pressed to the plasma membrane in a dark-adapted palisade cell.

images.caption: TEM of a shade orchid grown at 50, 30, 20 and 5 % light: dimmer light, taller and broader grana
images.credit: Shao et al. 2014, PLoS One 9:e85996, Fig. 6 (CC BY 4.0)
images.note: Anoectochilus roxburghii, a forest-floor herb; each row runs cell → chloroplast → grana (bars 5 µm, 0.5 µm, 0.2 µm).

images.caption: Chlorella photosynthesis per flash against flash intensity: the yield levels off at the brightest flashes
images.credit: Emerson & Arnold 1932, J Gen Physiol 16:191, Fig. 1 (p. 194)
images.note: Saturation is what makes the per-flash yield a count of units. Page scan from Internet Archive (Digital Library of India copy, item in.ernet.dli.2015.66762, leaf n204); cropped to figure and legend.

images.caption: CO₂ reduced per saturating flash rises in proportion to chlorophyll: 2480 chlorophylls per CO₂ molecule per flash
images.credit: Emerson & Arnold 1932, J Gen Physiol 16:191, Fig. 2 and text (p. 195)
images.note: The photosynthetic-unit number itself, in the authors’ words below the legend. They measured CO₂ reduced (manometrically), not O₂; leaf n205 of the same scan.

images.caption: Arabidopsis grown at 200, 600, 1800 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹: less LHCII (Lhcb1,2) and CP24 per PSII core in high light
images.credit: Bielczynski, Schansker & Croce 2016, Front Plant Sci 7:105, Fig. 3 (CC BY 4.0)
images.note: Optional antenna-size figure. The effect is modest here (Lhcb1,2 about −17 %, CP24 about −36 % from 200 to 1800); no true deep-shade treatment.

images.caption: Priestley 1774 frontispiece: pneumatic trough, a mouse under a jar, a plant sprig in an inverted jar (right)
